sentences.text: It is further submitted by Learned Senior Counsel that the present applicant-petitioner is a partnership firm and engaged in the business of retail sale of petroleum products under Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.(AOD) having its outlet at Motorstand, Agartala, since 1938.
The applicant-petitioner is a dealer of IOCL and the licence is granted by the authority in favour of IOCL.
On the basis of lease agreement in between the predecessors of the petitioners and IOCL, the petitioners are/were running the outlet on behalf of IOCL at Motorstand, Agartala.
But surprisingly all on a sudden the respondent No.3 issued Show Cause Notice on 23.09.2025 to the present applicant-petitioner.

On receipt of Show Cause Notice, the applicant-petitioner appeared and sought time but the authority did not consider the same rather on the same day issued another notice to the present applicant-petitioner for hearing under Section 152 of BNSS (Annexure-4) and in response to that the applicant-petitioner submitted one prayer to respondent No.3 on 25.09.2025 to supply copies of the documents like written representation submitted by some of the local inhabitants of Old Motorstand, Agartala on 08.09.2025 and the report of Inquiry Committee consisting of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar and Divisional Fire Officer, West Tripura, Agartala.

But the respondent No.3 did not consider the same rather by order dated 26.09.2025 cancelled the No Objection Certificate which ought to have been issued to the original licensee i.e. IOCL but the respondent No.3 without communicating anything to the IOCL cancelled the No Objection Certificate and communicated the order on 26.09.2025 to the present applicant- petitioner.

Learned Senior Counsel submitted that this retail outlet is the oldest outlet of the State and during the regime of Maharani this land was purchased and used for the purpose of retail outlet and earlier also the respondents-State did some arbitrary action and under compelling circumstances, the applicant-petitioner had to file one writ petition before this Court which was numbered as WP(C)
No.206 of 2011 and after hearing, a coordinate bench of this High Court by order dated 09.09.2016 cancelled the arbitrary order of the respondent-State and till date no appeal has been preferred by the respondent-authority challenging the said judgment.
Thus, the same has attained finality.

It was further submitted that in view of Rule 150 of Petroleum Rules, 2002, the No Objection Certificate has been cancelled by the authority but from the contents of Show Cause Notice(Annexure-3) and Hearing Notice(Annexure-4), there would be no whisper that the same was cancelled in view of Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002.

So, with an ulterior motive, the respondent No.3 has taken arbitrary action upon the petitioner and on the eve of Puja, their outlet has been closed resulting which the applicant-petitioner has sustained huge amount of financial losses and it is the only source of their earning
and if at this stage, the arbitrary action is not stayed by an order of the Court till disposal of the Writ Petition then the petitioner would be seriously prejudiced and it would be harsh to them.

On the other hand, Learned Advocate General appearing on behalf of the State-respondents No.1, 2 and 3 strongly countered the submission made by Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant-petitioner and submitted that this present writ petition is not maintainable and further submitted that the subject matter of WP(C) No.206 of 2011 is not similar to the present writ petition but the petitioner relying upon the said judgment is trying to make some cloud in the mind of the Court and on the basis of that judgment no relief can be granted in this case.

It was further M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85110784/
2 submitted that based on the representation of some of the local inhabitants, an enquiry was conducted through Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar and Divisional Fire Officer, West Tripura,
Agartala and on the basis of their reports, No Objection Certificate was cancelled by respondent No.3 by cancellation order dated 26.09.2025 and there was no infirmity or perversity in the said order.

sentences.text: It was further submitted by Learned Advocate General that considering the traffic movement and seriousness of the traffic congestion of that area, the respondent No.3 was compelled to issue Show Cause Notice from which it appears that the report of the Inquiring Authority was mentioned in the Show Cause Notice dated 23.09.2025(Annexure-3) and the findings of the Inquiring Authority was communicated to the present applicant- petitioner.
So at this stage there is no scope to take the plea on their behalf that no report was furnished to them.

In this regard, Learned Advocate General relied upon one citation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India Centre for Public Interest Litigation vs. Union of India & Ors., reported in (2013) 16 SCC 279 wherein in para No.25 and 26, Hon'ble the Apex Court observed as under:
"25.

sentences.text: We may emphasise that any food article which is hazardous or injurious to public health is a potential danger to the fundamental right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

A paramount duty is cast on the States and its authorities to achieve an appropriate level of protection to human life and health which is a fundamental right guaranteed to the citizens under Article 21 read with Article 47 of the Constitution of India.

26. We are, therefore, of the view that the provisions of the FSS Act and the PFA Act and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder have to be interpreted and applied in the light of the constitutional principles discussed above and endeavour has to be made to achieve an appropriate level of protection of human life and health.
Considerable responsibility is cast on the authorities as well as the other officers functioning under the abovementioned Acts to achieve the desired results.

The authorities are also obliged to maintain a system of control and other activities as appropriate to the circumstances, including public communication on food safety and risk, food safety surveillance and other monitoring activities covering all stages of food business."

Referring the same, Learned Advocate General drawn the attention of the Court that considering the public safety the order was issued by respondent No.3 and at this stage there is no scope to interfere with the said action of respondent No.3 (i.e. Annexure-6).

Ors. reported in (2014) 9 SCC 105 wherein in para No.21, 22 and 26, Hon'ble the Apex Court observed as under:

sentences.text: The central issue, however, pertains to the requirement of stating the action which is proposed to be taken.
The fundamental purpose behind the serving of show-cause notice is to make the noticee understand the precise case set up against him which he has to meet.
This would require the statement of imputations detailing out the alleged breaches and defaults he has committed, so that he gets an opportunity to rebut the same.
Another requirement, according to us, is the nature of action which is proposed to be taken for such a breach.

That should also be stated so that the noticee is able to point out that proposed action is not warranted in the given case, even if the defaults/breaches complained of are not satisfactorily explained.

When it comes to blacklisting, this requirement becomes all the more imperative,
having regard to the fact that it is harshest possible action.
22. The High Court has simply stated that the purpose of show-cause notice is primarily to enable the noticee to meet the grounds on which the action is proposed against him.
No doubt, the High Court is justified to this extent.
However, it is equally important to mention as to what would be the consequence if the noticee does not satisfactorily meet the grounds on which an action is proposed.
It is this second requirement which the High Court has failed to omit.

We may hasten to add that even if it is not specifically mentioned in the show-cause notice but it can clearly and safely be discerned from the reading thereof, that would be sufficient to meet this requirement.
26. In the present case, it is obvious that action is taken as provided in sub-clause (ii).
Under this clause, as is clear from the reading thereof, the Department had a right to cancel the contract and withhold the agreement.
That has been done.
The Department has also a right to get the job which was to be carried out by the defaulting contractor, to be carried out from other contractor(s).
In such an event, the Department also has a right to recover the difference from the defaulting contractor.
This clause, no doubt, gives further right to the Department to blacklist the contractor for a period of 4 years and also forfeit his earnest money/security deposit, if so required.
It is thus apparent that this sub-clause provides for various actions which can be taken and penalties which can be imposed by the Department.
In such a situation which action the Department proposes to take, need to be specifically stated in the show-cause notice.

It becomes all the more important when the action of blacklisting and/or forfeiture of earnest money/security deposit is to be taken, as the clause stipulates that such an action can be taken, if so warranted.

The words "if so warranted", thus,
assume great significance.

It would show that it is not necessary for the Department to resort to M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85110784/
4 penalty of blacklisting or forfeiture of earnest money/security deposit in all cases, even if there is such a power.

sentences.text: It is left to the Department to inflict any such penalty or not depending upon as to whether circumstances in a particular case warrant such a penalty.
There has to be due application of mind by the authority competent to impose the penalty, on these aspects.

Therefore, merely because of the reason that Clause 27 empowers the Department to impose such a penalty, would not mean that this specific penalty can be imposed, without putting the defaulting contractor to notice to this effect."

Referring the same, Learned Senior Counsel drawn the attention of this Court that on bare perusal of Rule 150 and Rule 152 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, it would be clear as to under what circumstances the No Objection Certificate can be cancelled.

But here in the Show Cause Notice nothing was reflected by the respondent No.3 regarding violation of Rule 150 of Petroleum Rules,
2002 and as such, the said order dated 29.06.2025(Annexure-6) is bad in law and cannot be sustained in the eye of law.

Learned Counsel, Ms. Paramita Dhar appearing on behalf of IOCL admitted the case of the applicant-petitioner and submitted that nothing was communicated to the respondent No.4 by the respondent No.3 in taking some prompt action without affording opportunity to the present applicant-petitioner.
Learned Counsel also admitted that the said respondent is the licensee and on the basis of lease agreement the present applicant-petitioner is running the outlet of the alleged petrol pump.
I have heard both the sides at length and perused the Writ Petition filed by the applicant-petitioner and the connected documents submitted with the Writ Petition.

Now, for the sake of convenience, I would like to refer the relevant Rule 150 and Rule 152 of Petroleum Rules, 2002 which provides as under:
"150. Cancellation of no-objection certificate.

(1) A no- objection certificate granted under rule 144 shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or the State Government, if the District Authority or the State Government is satisfied, that the licensee has ceased to have any right to use the site for storing petroleum:
Provided that before cancelling a no-objection certificate, the licensee shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sentences.text:
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1), an opportunity of being heard may not be given to the holder of a licence before his licence is suspended or cancelled in cases- (a) where the licence is suspended by a licensing authority as an interim measure for violation of any of the provisions of the Act or these rules, or of any conditions contained in such licence and in his opinion such violations is likely to cause imminent danger to the public:
Provided that where a licence is so suspended, the licensing authority shall give the holder of the licence an opportunity of being heard before the order of suspension is confirmed; or (b) where the licence is suspended or cancelled by the Central Government, if that Government considers that in the public interest or in the interest of the security of the State, such opportunity should not be given.

(3) A Licensing authority or the Central Government suspending or cancelling a licence under sub-rule (1), shall record its reason for so doing in writing and shall furnish to the licensee copy of the order cancelling the licence."
From the aforesaid rule, it appears that under what circumstances the State Government can cancel the No Objection Certificate but here in the case at hand the respondent No.3 could not project any case to invoke immediate action against the present applicant-petitioner and as such, the action on the part of respondent No.3 without affording adequate opportunity to the applicant-petitioner beyond the prescribed rule was harshest, whimsical and arbitrary for which Learned Senior Counsel urged for interference of the Court.

sentences.text: It is also on record that earlier some dispute cropped up and for which the present applicant-petitioner had to approach before this High Court and this High Court by order dated 09.09.2016 has cancelled the memo dated 10.05.2011 which was regarding shifting of the alleged petrol pump where it is situated now and the present issue is regarding cancellation of No Objection Certificate of the alleged petrol pump wherein the present applicant-petitioner is running the outlet since 1938.
Admittedly, the predecessor of the applicant-petitioner was the owner of the land which was leased out to IOCL on the basis of Lease agreement.
I have also gone through the citations referred by both the sides and perused the relevant Rule 150 and 152 of Petroleum Rules, 2002.
On perusal of Rule 150 of Petroleum Rules, 2002, it appears that under what circumstances No Objection Certificate can be cancelled.

On perusal of Show Cause Notice(Annexure-3) and Hearing Notice(Annexure-4) and subsequent cancellation of No Objection Certificate dated 26.09.2025 issued by D.M and collector, West Tripura, Agartala(Annexure-6), it appears to this Court at this stage that Annexure-6 was issued not in accordance with the statutory rules framed by the Authority.

Situated thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the petitioner has got a good prima facie case and accordingly, any action on "cancellation of No Objection Certificate" dated 26.09.2025 issued by the respondent No.3 be stayed till disposal of the writ petition.
With this observation, this present Interlocutory Application stands disposed of.
JUDGE MOUMITA Digitally signed by  MOUMITA DATTA DATTA
